messages.subject: question about identify() / plotly functionality
parts:
Hi everyone, I am completely new to ggtree but am considering using it for my project. I'm excited about all of the annotation functionality that it has, and I was wondering about the identify method of generating an interactive phylogenetic tree. 

I'm working on a meta-analysis of 18S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing data, and am phylogenetically placing these sequences into my reference tree to pull out the sequences that I'm interested in based on their phylogeny. I'm anticipating 1000s of sequences (not really sure on the amount, buy my reference tree has ~2000 sequences). What I want to be able to do is pull out the sequences I care about by highlighting them, and then output them either into a list of IDs, or use those to prune the tree. Is this possible using the idenitfy() method or by converting the tree to a plotly object? (also, if not, is anyone familiar with any other tools that might be of use? I'm interested in iTOL but most of the functionality I care about is behind a paywall)

Thank you!
